title: Lovran Cost Guide 2027: Hotels, Food, Transport
metaDescription: Lovran costs for 2027: rooms from about €60, bus to Opatija €3–4, tourist tax, meals and daily budgets for budget, mid-range and comfort travelers.
content:
## How Much Does a Trip to Lovran Cost?

Lovran is a small Kvarner Bay town of about 4,000 residents with a medieval old town and a seafront promenade. It sits roughly 6 km south of Opatija and is cheaper than Opatija for rooms and meals, though not cheap by Croatian standards. Prices peak from June to August and drop sharply in November through March.

### Daily budget per person (2 people sharing a room)

| Style | Daily cost | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Budget | €70–90 | Hostel or private room, bakery breakfast, one konoba meal, bus rides |
| Mid-range | €130–180 | 3-star hotel or apartment, two restaurant meals, beach and coffee stops |
| Comfort | €250+ | 4-star hotel or boutique stay, seafood dinner with wine, taxis |

These ranges assume summer or early autumn. In winter, subtract 25–40% from the accommodation portion.

## Accommodation Prices in Lovran

Booking platforms show about 95 hotels and many more apartments and guesthouses. Average nightly rates are roughly €155 in high season (June–August) and €85 in low season (December–February). November is typically the cheapest month. July is the most expensive, with averages close to €210 for a mid-range room.

### Budget (€27–70/night)

Hostel Link is the lowest-priced listed option, with beds from about €27. Small guesthouses and private apartments such as House Vali and Villa Nada start at roughly €60–80 for two in shoulder season. Villa Nada holds a 4.8 rating from guests.

### Mid-range (€70–140/night)

Hotel Lovran is a 3-star, 53-room property on the seafront promenade (Šetalište maršala Tita 19/2) with a private beach area and an on-site restaurant that non-guests can use. Standard rooms generally fall between €60 and €110. Hotel Excelsior, run by Liburnia Hotels & Villas on the same promenade, and Hotel Park, which has a spa and indoor pool, sit in a similar band at about €75–120. Hotel Villa Vera scores very highly with guests and costs about €120–140.

### Upper range (€140–250+/night)

Boutique Hotel Acacia starts around €135–150 and climbs toward €250+ in peak weeks. Hotel Villa Astra and Villa Ariston are also in this tier. Four-star hotels in Lovran average about €220–235 per night in booking data, while 3-star hotels average about €150 in summer.

### Tourist tax

Every overnight guest in Croatia pays a tourist tax of €0.65 to €2.65 per person per night, set by each town. Children under 12 are exempt and ages 12–18 pay half. Neighboring Opatija charges €2.20 from 1 April to 30 September and €1.50 the rest of the year. Lovran's rate falls in the same national range. Hotels list it as a separate line on the invoice, so check whether a quoted rate includes it.

## Food and Drink Costs

Lovran has a strong food reputation in the Kvarner region, and chestnuts, local lamb, and Kvarner seafood are the staples. Restaurants on the seafront promenade charge more than those in the old town streets.

- **Coffee:** about €1.80–2.50 for an espresso or macchiato.
- **Bakery breakfast** (burek, pastry and coffee): about €4–6.
- **Konoba main course** (pasta, risotto, grilled meat): typically €12–20.
- **Grilled fish or scampi:** often priced by weight, so a full seafood plate for one commonly reaches €25–40.
- **Local beer (0.5 L):** about €4–5. **Glass of Istrian or Kvarner wine:** €3.50–5.

Restaurants that regularly appear in visitor recommendations include Najade, Lovranska Vrata and Restaurant Knezgrad. Each is a short walk from the seafront hotels. Plan on €25–45 per person for a sit-down dinner with a drink at this type of restaurant.

**Insider tip:** Lunch menus and daily specials ("dnevni menu") at smaller konobas often cost €10–15 for a main course and soup. Eating the larger meal at midday and keeping dinner light cuts a daily food bill by about a third.

### Marunada chestnut festival

The Marunada festival takes place on weekends in October. Stalls sell roasted chestnuts, chestnut desserts and local wine, typically at €3–8 per item, and entry to the town is free. Hotel prices rise and rooms sell out well ahead, so book early if the dates matter.

## Getting There and Getting Around

Lovran is compact. The old town, the harbor and the main promenade can all be walked in under 15 minutes end to end, so most visitors spend nothing on local transport inside town.

### Bus from Opatija and Rijeka

Intercity buses between Lovran and Opatija cost about €3–4 one way and take 8–14 minutes. The first departures start around 7:00, and services run into the late evening. Buses to Rijeka take longer and cost more, with fares around €4–6 depending on operator. A taxi from Lovran to Opatija runs about €18–22 for the 6 km.

### From the airports

Rijeka Airport (on Krk island) is the closest, and a taxi to Lovran takes roughly 45–60 minutes. Pula and Zagreb airports are further out. Shared shuttle services from Opatija to Lovran can cost €31 or more, which is high for 6 km, so the regular bus is the better choice.

### Driving and parking

Parking in the town center is paid by zone, and rates rise in summer. Budget about €1–2 per hour near the promenade. Many hotels and apartments include parking or offer it for a daily fee, so ask before booking.

## Beaches, Activities and Free Things to Do

Lovran's beaches are pebble and concrete platforms with ladders into the water rather than sand. Public access is free in most places. Sun-lounger and umbrella rentals at managed beaches cost about €10–20 per set per day in summer. Hotel Lovran has a private beach area for guests.

The Lungomare coastal path connects Lovran with Opatija (about 12 km along the full route) and is free. The path also runs south toward Medveja. Walking the Lovran to Opatija stretch takes roughly 2.5–3 hours one way, and the bus back costs €3–4.

The old town, the harbor, the parish church of St. George and the main promenade cost nothing. Day trips to Mošćenice, the hill village above Lovran, and to Učka Nature Park add only fuel or taxi costs. Entry to Učka Nature Park viewpoints is inexpensive, with fees for specific sites usually only a few euros.

## Sample Budgets

### Weekend for two, shoulder season (May or September)

- 2 nights at a 3-star hotel: about €220
- Tourist tax: about €9
- Meals (two lunches, two dinners, breakfasts): about €170
- Bus and local costs: about €15
- **Total: about €415 for two**

### One week for two, July

- 7 nights in an apartment or mid-range hotel: about €840–1,200
- Tourist tax: about €31
- Food and drink: about €560–700
- Beach, transport, activities: about €100–150
- **Total: about €1,530–2,080 for two**

## Money-Saving Tips

1. **Travel in late May, June or September.** Water is warm enough for swimming and hotel rates are 30–40% below July and August.
2. **Book accommodation outside the seafront.** Rooms a 5–10 minute walk uphill cost less and are quieter.
3. **Use Lovran as a base instead of Opatija.** Room rates and restaurant prices are generally lower, and the bus covers the 6 km in under 15 minutes.
4. **Pay in cash at small konobas and bakeries.** Most accept cards, but a few smaller places in the old town still prefer cash.
5. **Choose Sunday check-ins when possible.** Booking data shows Sunday as the cheapest night to stay.

The seafront promenade restaurants are the weakest value in town. The terrace views are pleasant, but the same dish in a side-street konoba usually costs €3–6 less and tastes at least as good.

## Practical Information

- **Currency:** euro (€). Croatia has used it since 2023.
- **Cards:** accepted at hotels, most restaurants and shops. Carry some cash for small purchases and market stalls.
- **Tipping:** not mandatory. Rounding up or leaving 5–10% for good service is common.
- **Best value months:** April, May, late September, and November, when prices are lowest.
- **Busiest period:** July to mid-August, plus October weekends during Marunada.

faq.question: Is Lovran expensive?
faq.answer: Lovran is mid-priced for the Croatian coast. It is cheaper than neighboring Opatija but pricier than inland Istria. Expect €60–130 for a double room outside July and August and €12–20 for a konoba main course.

faq.question: How much does a hotel in Lovran cost per night?
faq.answer: A 3-star hotel averages roughly €85–150 depending on season, and 4-star hotels average about €220–235. Budget guesthouses and hostel beds start from around €27–60. July is the most expensive month and November is the cheapest.

faq.question: How much is the tourist tax in Lovran?
faq.answer: Croatian tourist tax ranges from €0.65 to €2.65 per person per night depending on the town and season. Neighboring Opatija charges €2.20 in high season (April–September) and €1.50 the rest of the year. Children under 12 are exempt, and ages 12–18 pay half.

faq.question: How much is the bus from Lovran to Opatija?
faq.answer: A one-way ticket costs about €3–4 and takes 8–14 minutes. Buses start around 7:00 and run into the late evening. A taxi for the same 6 km costs about €18–22.

faq.question: How much does a meal cost in Lovran?
faq.answer: A konoba main course is usually €12–20, and grilled fish or scampi can reach €25–40 per person. Coffee costs about €1.80–2.50. A sit-down dinner with a drink typically totals €25–45 per person.

faq.question: What is a good daily budget for Lovran?
faq.answer: Budget travelers can manage on €70–90 per person per day, and mid-range travelers should plan on €130–180. A comfort-level trip with a boutique hotel and seafood dinners starts around €250. These figures assume summer or early autumn.

faq.question: When is the cheapest time to visit Lovran?
faq.answer: November through March has the lowest hotel rates, with average prices about 40% below summer. Late May and September offer the best balance of warm weather and moderate prices. Avoid October weekends if the Marunada chestnut festival would push rates up.

quickAnswer: Lovran costs about €70–90 per person per day on a budget, €130–180 mid-range, and €250+ at the top end. Double rooms run roughly €60–130 in shoulder season and up to €170+ in July and August. Bus rides to Opatija cost €3–4. Tourist tax is added per night.
